title: Minimum Cuts to Divide a Circle
summary: A valid cut in a circle is either a diameter or a radius.
statement: A valid cut in a circle is either a diameter or a radius. For a given integer n, determine the least number of cuts required to divide the circle into n equal segments.
constraints: Cuts are straight lines across the circle.
Return the minimum number of cuts; one sector requires no cut.
hints: Handle n=1 separately with zero cuts.
For even n, each diameter contributes two opposite sector boundaries.
For odd n, no boundary can be paired with an opposite one, so use n radii; return n/2 for even n.
Opposite boundaries coincide on one straight cut exactly in the even case, establishing both constructions and lower bounds.
editorial: Opposite boundaries coincide on one straight cut exactly in the even case, establishing both constructions and lower bounds.

tests.explanation: Two perpendicular diameter cuts produce four equal sectors.
Three radius cuts from the center are needed for three equal sectors.
